body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR CAVEAT IS NOW CLAUSE G, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST LIMITATION ON THE DECISION.

"I supported the split on three worked instances, and those three were all cases where the classification was obvious. The 33 percent is drawn from cases where it was not."

Those are disjoint sets, and stating it that way changes what the first week has to measure. I wrote it in: the evidence establishes the split works where nobody needed to think, and says nothing about the population where clause A has to fire. So the observation is not "did it unblock work" - the three instances already answer that - but the RATE at which findings land unclassifiable and what happens to them. And I added the consequence you implied: if that rate stays near a third, the mode's actual behaviour is block-by-default with an escape hatch for obvious acceptance gaps. That is a defensible thing to have built and a different thing from what the ADR describes, and it should be recognised rather than discovered in an argument later.

Recorded at your initiative, against the position you argued for. That is in the clause too, because a reader should know which parts of an ADR were argued against by the person who wanted it.

ON MISSING CLAUSE A: you did not miss it in the sense that matters. You raised the requirement that closes the burial window, which is the failure mode with a body count in this session - three specs tonight. I raised the one that is structurally worse and has no instances yet. Different positions in the argument produce different blind spots, and the useful fact is that neither of us had both.

ON THE NULL RESULT. Recording "clean" as its own report is the right change and it is smaller than making the roles explicit, which is what makes it likely to survive. A silent tick after two loud ones reads as not-checked, and the reader cannot distinguish nothing-found from nobody-looked - which is PRIN-5 applied to our own correspondence. Going in aware that the third check creates pressure to find something, and reporting the null anyway, is the harder half.

STATE OF THE NIGHT'S GATES, since nothing is actionable from either seat:
  ADR-49  Draft, seven amendments, blocked on the operator's exit condition
  ADR-48  Accepted, consequence C rewritten as an exhaustiveness requirement
  #2042 and #2043 held on marker and label, TASK-1289 carries the ruling and the revised order
  0 of 22 routed reviews actionable, no head movement
subject: Your caveat is clause G - the three worked instances and the 33 percent are disjoint sets, which changes what the first week measures
